Optimal.Notes: A slight bump to texture and world detail quality over MaxBattery with a modest TDP increase gives a noticeably better-looking image while still holding 30 fps on most maps. Keep spawned vehicles at 2 or fewer to avoid CPU physics bottlenecks.

profiles.Summary: BeamNG.drive is an extremely demanding soft-body physics simulator that pushes the Steam Deck hard — the Deck's GPU sits well below even the minimum spec (RX 570 / GTX 1060 with 6 GB VRAM), and the CPU-heavy physics calculations compound the challenge. Expect 25–35 fps at low settings with significant variation based on map complexity and the number of vehicles spawned.
profiles.BasisNote: No Deck-specific player reports were available; profiles are estimated from the PC minimum/recommended requirements and the Deck's RDNA 2 GPU being well below spec. On your first run, check the frame rate on the main menu map and in a free-roam session — switch to Max Battery if fps drops below 25 or the device runs hot.

MaxBattery.Notes: Limiting to a single vehicle and rendering at 960x600 with FSR upscaling is essential to keep both CPU physics load and GPU load manageable at this TDP. Avoid large open-world maps like Italy; smaller test environments or short tracks are far more stable.

KnownIssues: BeamNG.drive's minimum GPU requirement (6 GB VRAM) exceeds what the Deck can realistically dedicate from its 16 GB shared pool, leading to stutters in complex scenes or with mods loaded.
The game's CPU-side soft-body physics is very demanding and can bottleneck the Deck's Zen 2 cores, especially with multiple vehicles spawned simultaneously.
No native Linux build exists; Proton is required, and some launcher or UI steps may need keyboard/mouse input.
Frame rate can drop sharply when entering dense traffic or large open-world maps — reducing spawned vehicles is the single most effective mitigation.

MaxPerformance.Notes: Running uncapped GPU clocks at full 15 W TDP can approach 40 fps on simpler maps with one or two vehicles, but expect dips to 30 fps or below on complex maps or with traffic. Thermal throttling may reduce the GPU clock after extended play sessions.

Optimal.Notes: 40 Hz refresh with a matching frame cap gives smooth, tear-free physics feel at a reasonable power cost; FSR from 1024x640 keeps the image acceptably sharp. Stick to single-vehicle play and avoid the largest open maps to hold the target framerate.
